name: Deep Turtle Green
lede: Deep Turtle Green is a muted, yellow-leaning green, named for the animal rather than a plant.

sections.title: A shell, not a leaf
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 nomenclature places the swatch at plate XXXII, hue 31′′, and the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 reads it as a strong yellowish green, several units from the block center [1]. Our library files the name among animal words rather than plant words, alongside other shell- and hide-toned greens [1].

The nearest named color in our data is [[dusty-green]], about 6.5 units off, with [[boa]], [[malachite-green]] and [[sage]] close behind [2]. All sit in the same soft, grey-yellow-green range as sage and moss.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The archive finds this color, as photographed, in 70 of 23,781 paintings, rarer than 53 percent of the named colors we track [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 12 of 1,674 paintings, at 0.7 per cent of that century's paintings, 3.8 times the overall rate [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays an accent [3]. It is also over-represented in Impressionist work, at 6 of 140 paintings, 5.1 times the overall rate [3]. The earliest match is a 1513 painting, 399 years before Ridgway's 1912 record, so this is a look-alike hue in an old photograph, not a pigment identification, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3].

issues: Fixed: the field-notes paragraph invented a painter claim ("Gustav Klimt, 6 of 50 sampled paintings"; "Vincent van Gogh's Girl in White, 1890") with no basis — ar.pa and ar.pn are both empty for this slug. The peak-decade stat (1910s, 1.9%, 8.4x) does not match any real field (century fact is 1900s/0.7%/3.8x; the raw pd field is 1890/0.9%/4.2x) and the earliest-match sentence named a '1600 Mughal court painting' that isn't in the data (first-seen is an unattributed 1513 painting; 1600 is only the third-earliest). Rewrote from the real presence, century, role, movement (Impressionism) and first-seen facts, and swapped the decade-trivia question for one on the movement fact. Removed the unsupported painter and attribution claims rather than inventing replacements.
